title: colab-browser: consent clicks both Drive-for-desktop screens; Chrome's own opener; popups command
description: Live failure: after Continue on 'signing back in to Google Drive for desktop', Google showed a second screen in the same window ('Google Drive for desktop wants access to your Google Account'). consent did not match it, the mount timed out (ValueError: mount failed) and the runtime idled about 14 min. Also: Playwright's opener() is sometimes null on connectOverCDP, so consent refused with '0 Google sign-in windows were opened by this tab', and sign-in windows left from failed mounts piled up. Fix: match both screens and click through them in one consent call, refuse screens with unticked access boxes, read the opener from Chrome (Target.getTargets), a guarded fallback when no opener is recorded, newest window wins, and a popups [--close] command. Docs: don't reload mid-mount, timeout_ms=600000 when a person may click.
close_reason: Pushed; live check is the next pi05 relaunch

title: colab-browser: CLI-first (official google-colab-cli): kernel-side self-releasing jobs, sessions watchdog, agent-driven CLI sign-in; browser as fallback
colab-browser: close the notebook's tab and any Drive page when the job is finished
description: The finish step releases the runtime and copies the results but never closes the tab, and the traps table only warns that closing a tab doesn't stop billing, which reads as 'keep tabs open'. On a shared machine an agent-driven browser kept five notebooks with no runtime and two Drive pages open for a day; Drive pages grew to about 3G of JS heap each, and the browser held more than 20G of RAM that other work couldn't use. Fix: step 7 closes the notebook's tab and any Drive page the agent opened, after the runtime is gone and the results are copied; a traps row says why.
close_reason: Step 7 closes the notebook's tab and any Drive page; traps row added; rehearsed old vs new
